scenes.headline: Spark Architecture
scenes.subtitle: How the driver, cluster manager, and executors work together.
scenes.narration: Every Spark application is built from three cooperating pieces: a driver, a cluster manager, and a set of executors.

scenes.headline: The three roles
items: Driver — the brain that plans and coordinates the job
Cluster manager — hands out CPU and memory resources
Executors — the workers that actually process partitions
Tasks — the smallest unit of work sent to executors
scenes.narration: The driver is the brain that plans and coordinates the job. The cluster manager hands out CPU and memory. Executors are the workers that process data partitions, and tasks are the smallest units of work sent to those executors.

scenes.headline: From submit to result
scenes.narration: When you submit an application, the driver builds a plan and asks the cluster manager for resources. The manager launches executors, which run tasks on their partitions, and results flow back to the driver.

scenes.headline: Where your code runs
scenes.code:
spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("App").getOrCreate()
# Runs on the DRIVER: builds the plan
df = spark.read.parquet("/data/sales")
# Runs on EXECUTORS: distributed work
df.groupBy("region").sum("amount").show()
scenes.narration: The SparkSession setup and plan construction run on the driver. The actual heavy lifting of the group-by and sum runs out on the executors across the cluster, and only the final result returns to the driver.

scenes.text: The driver thinks, executors do the work, and the cluster manager provides the resources.
scenes.narration: In short, the driver thinks, the executors do the work, and the cluster manager provides the resources that make it all possible.
